subject: Post-call: encryption & residency clarifications + next steps
messages:
From: Priyom Das <priyom.das@redwood.ai>
To: Lena Ortiz <lena.ortiz@novushealth.com>
Cc: Dev Patel <dev.patel@redwood.ai>, Camila Reyes <camila.reyes@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 30 Jun 2026 14:12:00 +0000
Subject: Post-call: encryption & residency clarifications + next steps

Hi Lena — thanks again for taking the time today. Quick recap of the items we discussed and a proposed set of next steps so we can keep momentum on the procurement lane. Please confirm or correct anything below.

Summary of your priorities from today:
- Data residency: EU-only (eu-west-1) for all production traffic and long-term storage.
- PII handling: customer-identifiable data must be redacted or tokenized on ingestion; Novus will share a sample field set.
- Retention: default request/interaction logs retained for 12 months; short-term token cache retention limited to 30 days unless otherwise agreed.
- Logging/audit: per-request audit trail (request-id, timestamp, model-id, worker-id) forwarded to your SIEM; ability to disable content logging for selected routes.
- Encryption: in-transit TLS 1.3 mandatory; at-rest AES-256-GCM for model and persisted stores. You prefer customer-managed keys (CMEK/BYOK) backed by HSM (CloudHSM or On-prem HSM) for key custody and rotation.

Attachments I’m including: redwood-sec-questionnaire.pdf (answers to the 80% of your security Qs); I also referenced the internal draft arch diagram we discussed (I’ll share a link once it’s cleaned up).

Open clarifying questions for you (so we can size the Dedicated/Private options correctly):
1) Which Key Management service do you want to use for CMEK? Options we support out of the box: AWS KMS (CloudHSM-backed), Azure Key Vault (HSM), or your own on-prem HSM with VPN peering.
2) Do you require network isolation via VPC-only Private deployment (no public egress) or is VPC Peering / PrivateLink to a Redwood Hosted endpoint sufficient for an initial pilot?
3) For audit log redundancy: do you want us to push CloudTrail-like logs to your S3 (preferred), or ship via syslog/Splunk/Datadog?

Next steps I propose:
- Novus: share the sample PII schema and the filled Data Handling worksheet (you mentioned an internal spreadsheet).
- Redwood: Camila to prepare a short technical brief on CMEK options + HSM variants and an updated arch sketch reflecting EU residency. Dev to prepare an initial sizing/estimate for a Dedicated pool + HSM add-on.
- Schedule: 30–45 minute technical deep-dive next week with your security engineer and our Camila/Dev.

If that looks right, please reply with answers to Q1–Q3 and a few windows for the deep-dive. I’ll get the brief and estimates ready once I have your confirmation.

Thanks — Priyom

--
Priyom Das
Enterprise Sales, Redwood Inference
priom.das@redwood.ai | +1 415-555-0148

Subject: Re: Post-call: encryption & residency clarifications + next steps

Priyom — thanks for the clear recap. Confirming the high level is correct. A few specifics: 

- Key management: we run primarily in AWS (eu-west-1). Preferred approach is AWS KMS with keys in CloudHSM (we have an existing CloudHSM cluster we’d like to use if possible). If that is incompatible with your hosted option we need a plan for Private deployment with HSM integration.
- Network: pilot can start with PrivateLink to a Redwood-hosted cluster in eu-west-1 for faster time-to-value. For production we require VPC-only Private deployment (no internet egress) and support for NAT-less egress to our telemetry collectors.
- Retention: 12 months for request logs; direct PII outputs should never be stored persistently unless explicitly captured by business flows (we will flag those).
- Logs: push audit logs to our S3 bucket (we’ll provide a write-only bucket and an IAM role). We also use Splunk for SIEM — a forwarder is fine as long as PII is stripped per our rules.

I’m attaching an excerpt of our data handling spreadsheet (Novus-Data-Handling-Reqs.xlsx). I’ll loop in our security engineer for the call; possible windows next Tue/Wed (5–7 Jul).

Best,
Lena Ortiz
Head of Product Security, Novus Health
Lena.Oritz@novushealth.com

Quick technical notes (draft) — sending what I can before I finish the brief: 

1) CMEK/Custody options we support today:
   - AWS KMS (CloudHSM-backed keys): supported for Private deployment and for Dedicated with customer key import/authorization; hosted API has constraints around direct CloudHSM integration (we can do envelope encryption with customer-managed wrapping keys but full CloudHSM control requires Private).
   - AWS CloudHSM / On-prem HSM: we can integrate via VPN/VPC peering for Private deployments; supports HSM-backed key generation and hardware rotation policies.
   - Azure Key Vault: supported via service principal and key wrapping for Dedicated/Private.

2) Recommended pattern: envelope encryption (data keys generated per-tenant, wrapped by the customer CMK). Redwood stores only wrapped data keys and enforces strict in-memory-only unwrapping on compute nodes. Key rotation: we support periodic re-wrap and emergency rotation workflows that rotate data keys and perform replay-safe rekeying.

3) Audit & logging:
   - Key usage events can be surfaced via CloudTrail / audit bundle and pushed to customer S3 (we can push hourly bundles).
   - Application-level request logs (request-id, route, model, latency, worker-id) can be exported to S3 and/or forwarded to Splunk. 
   - PII handling: we have pre-ingest hooks for field-level redaction/tokenization; recommend combining client-side tokenization for sensitive fields with server-side redaction to minimize exposure.

4) Gaps / blockers to call out now:
   - Hosted (public) product cannot offer exclusive HSM control in our multitenant clusters. For full HSM-backed CMEK where the customer holds the HSM, we need Private deployment.
   - For production VPC-only deployments, we need a networking runbook from Novus (CIDR ranges, peering model, NAT requirements, S3 endpoints).

I’ll attach the finished brief (cmk-options-brief.pdf) and an arch sketch; both will include code-level notes for our infra team.

Camila
